state.claim_text: The Ridgeway Rainshell is fully waterproof and comes in every size from XS to 4XL.
state.supplied_evidence: Ridgeway product spec sheet, rev 3: the shell fabric is rated water-resistant; seams are not taped and the garment is not rated or tested as waterproof. Size run: XS, S, M, L, and XL are in production now; 2XL through 4XL are planned for the following season.

rationale: The waterproof part of the claim is incompatible with evidence stating the garment is not waterproof, while the size part is supported only in a narrower form (XS through XL). The contract's precedence rule says a claim that is partly contradicted and partly narrower is contradicted, not overstated.

state.classification_rule: Promotional content advertises or offers any product, service, discount, event, upgrade, or membership, including a link whose purpose is to sell. Transactional content confirms, changes, or delivers something the recipient already asked for or is owed: order status, receipts, delivery updates, password resets, account or safety notices, and how to report a problem with an order.
state.message_text: Your Northwick Cycles order NC-4471 has shipped and should arrive on Thursday. You can follow the parcel at northwick.example/track. Reply to this message if anything about the order looks wrong.

rationale: Every part of the message delivers order status or a way to report a problem, which the rule defines as transactional, and nothing offers or advertises anything.

state.classification_rule: Promotional content is any text that offers the recipient a discount code, a sale price, a coupon, or a limited-time price reduction. Transactional content is any text that confirms, updates, or completes an order, delivery, or account action the recipient already initiated. Text that does neither is not covered by this rule.
state.message_text: Good news: your Cobblewick order has shipped and should arrive on Thursday. While you wait, have a look at our new autumn arrivals at cobblewick.example/autumn; the wool throws are our favourites this year. If you need to change your delivery address, reply to this message before Wednesday noon.

rationale: The shipping confirmation and the address-change instruction are transactional under the rule, and the new-arrivals plug offers no discount code, sale price, coupon, or price reduction, so under the supplied definition it is not promotional even though general marketing sense would call it one. The contract requires applying only the supplied rule, and every part the rule addresses is transactional.

state.copy_text: Picture the last time you stood waiting for a kettle. Now ask yourself what you could have done with those four minutes. Keep reading and we will show you how the Quillstone kettle brings a litre to a rolling boil in ninety seconds, why its handle stays cool to the touch, and what our engineers gave up to make it happen. rationale: Every imperative here (picture, ask yourself, keep reading) invites the reader to imagine something or to continue within the copy itself. The contract counts only requests to do something outside the copy, so none of these is a call to action despite the imperative mood.

state.audience_persona: Owner-operator of an independent neighbourhood bakery with three to eight staff. Runs the counter during the morning rush, then does the books alone at the kitchen table after close. Talks about 'the register', 'wholesale accounts', and 'the morning rush'. Needs invoicing for wholesale accounts to take less of the evening; there is no separate finance or management staff.
state.copy_text: You know the feeling: the morning rush is over, the register is counted, and a stack of wholesale invoices is still waiting for you at the kitchen table. Loafline drafts and sends them while you sleep. Ask your finance team to set up approval tiers so regional managers can sign off invoices from any of your locations before they go out.

rationale: The opening speaks directly to the persona's situation and vocabulary, but the final sentence presumes a finance team, regional managers, and multiple locations that the persona explicitly does not have. The contract says copy that addresses the persona in one part and presumes a different reader in another is addresses_different_reader.

state.voice_guide: Tallow & Wick writes like a friendly neighbour: warm, plain-spoken, and in the second person. Show at least one of those traits in every piece. Rules: never use exclamation marks; never write in all capitals; never use the words 'cheap', 'guaranteed', or 'revolutionary' anywhere in copy, including inside negations, questions, or quoted testimonials.
state.copy_text: You light a candle to make a room feel like yours, not to impress anyone. That is why we pour ours in small batches and price them fairly. We will not call them cheap, because they are not; we will just say they are worth what you pay, and that we hope your evenings feel a little softer for it.

rationale: The copy clearly shows the guide's warm, plain-spoken, second-person traits, but it uses the banned word 'cheap' inside a negation, which the guide explicitly says still counts as use. The contract selects off_voice whenever a stated rule is broken, even when described traits are also present.

state.copy_text: Moving to Sundial from Northbeam takes one click: our importer carries over every project, board, and comment. 'Northbeam kept crashing on us during quarterly planning; Sundial has not gone down once in eight months,' says Ada Ferrin, operations lead at Kestrel Labs. Sundial also connects to Ledgerly and Inkwell inboxes out of the box.

rationale: The migration sentence on its own would be a neutral reference, and an attributed quotation counts as neutral only when it carries no assertion of superiority or inferiority; this quotation asserts that Northbeam is worse (it crashes) and Sundial better. Because a comparative claim applies, the contract's stated order puts comparative_claim ahead of neutral_reference.
